newsitem.title: USA: USDA coffee crop estimates seen neutral to bearish.
newsitem.headline: USDA coffee crop estimates seen neutral to bearish.

text.p: U.S. coffee futures may ease a bit in response to a slight increase in the USDA's world production estimate, but the overall reaction to the numbers is expected to be muted, traders and analysts said.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture's semi-annual world crop report, released after the close of trading on Friday, pegged global production for 1996/97 at 100.9 60-kg million bags, up 1.8 million from the 99.1 million bags seen in the June forecast.
"Overall, I think the estimate will be viewed as neutral to a little bearish," said one analyst. "There was no major revision on the production side."
The USDA revised its 1996/97 crop estimate for top-grower Brazil to 27.0 million bags, down from 27.5 million bags in June.
"It is probably a little bearish," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "There is more coffee around even if there is less Brazilian coffee."
While some traders were a bit surprised by the downward revision for Brazil's, the biggest jolt came from surprisingly strong Mexican and Central American yields.
Traders had expected to see lower forecasts for Mexico and some Central American countries, following heavy rainfall and flooding in the region in October.
The USDA pegged Mexico's output at 5.4 million bags, up from 4.7 million bags forecast in June, while Guatemala's coffee crop increased to 3.93 million bags from 3.5 million bags.
Costa Rica's production was revised slightly, dipping to 2.5 million bags from 2.55 million bags.
Elsewhere, number-two grower Colombia's 1996/97 coffee output was pegged at 12.5 million bags, unchanged from a revised USDA estimate published last month.
As expected, robusta coffee crops from Indonesia and Vietman were raised.
"There was no surprise in the Indonesia or Vietnam crops," an analyst said. "The bulk of the increases came from robustas which should pressure London futures."

In the report, USDA predicted Indonesia's 1996/97 production would increase to 7.5 million bags, from the 6.5 million seen in June. By comparison, Indonesia's drought-hit 95/96 crop totalled 6.0 million bags.
Vietnam's 1996/97 coffee crop was forecast to come in at 4.3 million bags, up from 3.5 million bags seen previously, the USDA said.
